entry_conditions: Two finite causal frames place the TCP locally near a demonstrated approach, grasp, lift, or carry relation. The source is upright and ungrasped or visibly co-moving with closed fingers, and measured joints can reach the local target.
exit_conditions: Closed fingers and source/TCP co-motion are visible, the source is table-clear, and it is staged upright above the bowl near the demonstrated high handoff relation.
overlap_role: Actions [180,360) remain action-supervised in this policy and controlled_pour_and_right, teaching local lift, upright carry, bowl staging, and the first small tilt.
successor_readiness: The successor may receive after a closed, co-moving and clearly lifted source; nominal switching occurs at high bowl staging.
failure_signatures: Repeated local motion without reducing handle error, open fingers at lift, source/TCP motion disagreement, particle separation before secure lift, IK nonconvergence, or joint-limit contact. None is a demonstrated recovery mode.
continuation_guidance: Preserve two-frame history across switches and compose every represented slot with the fresh measured TCP. Monitor physical co-motion rather than treating closure as contact. Use the source-frame policy for large source displacement and the phase-aware policy when grasp/lift phase is ambiguous.
limitations: The successful demonstrations do not establish correction from unseen perturbations. Body-frame increments can accumulate diffusion error, and reachability, collision clearance, contact, large source rotations, and slips remain unsupported.
